actions.operation: Resolve interference by modifying geometry and/or position so the handle and coffeepot no longer intersect

parameters.edit_strategy: Prefer modify handle (U-bracket) over coffeepot to preserve coffeepot function; use local relief first, global offset second

actions.target: Handle and coffeepot (their solid bodies / contacting regions)
actions.relational_constraint: No collision/intersection between handle and coffeepot (separated geometry); applies to the region 'between' the two parts where interference occurs
actions.unresolved_reference: Coffeepot solid is not defined in model.json (only housing/handle/cord/etc. are defined). Exact interfering faces and required clearance are not explicitly given. Use assembly interference detection to identify contact faces on the handle (likely the bracket inner skin and/or side cheeks) and then apply a minimum clearance gap (suggest 2.0 mm unless otherwise specified).
steps: Interference localization (assembly-level): Insert/activate the coffeepot component in the assembly with the dispenser housing. Run an interference/clearance analysis between the coffeepot body and the external U-handle/guard bracket body (Section S03). Record the interfering region coordinates and identify which handle faces participate (most likely S03: face_code 0011 Bracket inner skin / FACE 366, and/or face_code 0015 & 0017 inner cheek planes / FACE 364 & FACE 372).

Decide modification ownership (design intent): Prefer modifying the handle/guard bracket (S03) rather than the coffeepot because (1) S03’s function intent includes providing clearance/protection around the housing, (2) S03 is an accessory frame that can accept a relief without impacting internal module S05, and (3) altering the coffeepot risks ergonomic/functional constraints. Only modify coffeepot geometry if it is a standardized purchased part and the handle must remain unchanged.

Primary fix (local relief cut on handle inner side, preserves outer appearance): If collision occurs on the bracket inner skin (face_code 0011 / FACE 366) at the mid-height band corresponding to the bracket flange zone (y≈279.40 to 304.80 from faces 0012/0013), create a local pocket/relief on the handle inner surface: (a) Create a reference plane normal to the coffeepot axis (typically parallel to the bracket cheek planes) positioned through the centroid of the interference volume; alternatively use one cheek inner plane as a sketch plane (face_code 0015 on right and 0017 on left). (b) Project the interfering silhouette of the coffeepot onto this sketch plane; offset the projected profile outward by the desired clearance_gap_mm (e.g., 2.0 mm) to create a 'keep-out' boundary. (c) Use an Extrude-Cut (or Boolean Subtract using the coffeepot + offset as a tool body) to remove material from the handle bracket toward the outer side, limiting the cut depth to what is necessary to clear the coffeepot while maintaining minimum wall thickness of the handle. (d) Add internal fillets along the cut edges (manufacturability + stress reduction) and ensure tangency where the cut meets the BSPLINE inner skin to avoid sharp corners and stress risers.

Secondary fix (move/offset face for global clearance if local relief is insufficient): If the collision spans a large arc of the U-bracket, use direct modeling 'Move Face/Offset Face' on the bracket inner skin (face_code 0011 / FACE 366): (a) Select face 0011 and all tangentially connected inner faces of the bracket in the collision band (likely including adjacent minor faces FACE 367/369). (b) Apply an offset away from the coffeepot by a value determined from interference results + clearance_gap_mm. (c) Heal/extend adjacent surfaces so the bracket remains watertight and preserves continuity into the bottom/top bracket flange planes (face_code 0012 / FACE 370 and face_code 0013 / FACE 368). (d) Verify that the bracket outer skin (face_code 0010 / FACE 365) remains acceptable aesthetically; if thickness becomes too thin, revert and instead widen the bracket by offsetting the outer skin outward and reblending.

Cheek-specific relief (if collision is on side cheeks rather than the U-arc): If interference is localized near the side cheek inner faces (face_code 0015 right inner cheek plane / FACE 364, and/or face_code 0017 left inner cheek plane / FACE 372), create a cheek cutout: (a) Sketch on the offending cheek inner plane (0015 and/or 0017). (b) Project coffeepot interfering outline to the plane; offset by clearance_gap_mm. (c) Extrude-Cut through the cheek thickness up to (but not through) the outer cheek plane (face_code 0014 / FACE 363 on right, face_code 0016 / FACE 371 on left) if you must preserve outside silhouette; otherwise cut through and add a bezel/cover feature later. (d) Add fillets/chamfers on the cut perimeter for durability and appearance. (e) Mirror the cheek relief about the X=0 midplane if the coffeepot and intended clearance are symmetric.

Preserve attachment constraints (S04 interfaces): After any handle modification, validate that the pivot/fastener interfaces (Section S04: countersink cones 0018/0020 and cylinders 0019/0021; plus cylinder extensions 0022/0023 if present) are not altered in a way that changes screw seating, coaxiality, or clamp face integrity. If any relief intersects these features, adjust the relief boundary to maintain a no-edit keepout around S04 faces (at least the countersink and the primary attachment cylinders).

Validation: Re-run interference check to confirm zero intersection and confirm the minimum clearance gap is achieved everywhere along the coffeepot insertion/removal path. Also check handle strength: ensure remaining ligament thickness and local radii are sufficient; add reinforcing ribs only if needed and only in non-interfering regions.

Documentation/update: Note the final clearance value, edited faces, and whether the change was local relief vs global offset. Ensure both left and right sides remain consistent with the product’s symmetry intent unless asymmetry is required by coffeepot/cord routing.

intention: Eliminate physical interference between the handle and the coffeepot so the parts do not collide in the model/assembly.
Maintain functional assembly insertion/removal of the coffeepot while preserving handle strength, attachment integrity (S04), and external appearance of the bracket (S03).
